description: traffiQ, the local public transport authority of Frankfurt am Main, publishes passenger counts for the city's underground, tram and bus lines. For each line and survey year the list gives the busiest cross-section on an average weekday and the total passengers in both directions, with aggregated loads for some important sections. Up to 2019 the figures come from manual counts at more than 50 stops on undisturbed midweek days in the fourth quarter; counts paused in 2020 and 2021, and since 2022 an automatic passenger counting system, fitted to 15% of vehicles and deployed so that each trip is counted at least twice, provides the data. Two XLSX files cover 2010 to 2019 and 2022 to 2025. Coverage is Frankfurt's local public transport; regional trains, S-Bahn and regional buses are counted by the RMV. Access: free under the Data Licence Germany Attribution 2.0, including commercial use. Caveats: the survey method and season changed in 2022, route changes can break a line's series, and 2022 and 2023 were still affected by the pandemic. It supports calibration of public transport demand and capacity models and service planning, and complements the Mobility Database and the German MobiData BW catalogued here.
